processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Compression sample heated to 1200 °C at 10 °C/s prior to homogenization.
Homogenized by holding for 120 s at 1200 °C.
Cooled from 1200 °C to the set deformation temperature of 950 °C at 5 °C/s.
Held for 15 s at the set temperature before compression so the temperature difference between inside and outside of the sample is the same.

Isothermal constant-strain-rate compression to 60% reduction (maximum true strain 0.92) at a strain rate of 0.01 s^-1 on a Gleeble-3500 thermo-mechanical simulator; mica foils with high-temperature lubricant applied to both end faces.
After compression the sample was sprayed with water to cool it down.

structures.overall_structure: Initial (as-forged billet) microstructure of the Fe-Mn-Al-C steel used as the pre-deformation reference state: large polygonal grains delimited by bright etched boundaries, with dark grain interiors containing abundant fine, closely spaced, parallel light-grey striations (segregation banding) whose direction changes from grain to grain, indicating chemical heterogeneity.

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: Grains are large relative to the 100 µm scale bar — individual grains span roughly one to a few times the bar length.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: cylindrical sample of Φ8 mm × 12 mm
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Isothermal constant-strain-rate hot compression to 60% (true strain 0.92) using a Gleeble-3500 thermo-mechanical simulator; mica foils with high-temperature lubricant applied to both end faces; compressed sample split in half along the axial axis for metallography.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: After splitting the compressed sample in half along the axial axis, followed by sample preparation, grinding, polishing and etching with 30% nitric acid alcohol solution (volume fraction).
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe and compare the microstructure/deformation-zone morphology of the hot-compressed Fe-Mn-Al-C steel specimens.
characterization_methods.key_findings: Microstructure images collected for compressed samples (e.g. Fig. 9 optical micrographs with 100 µm scale bars).

computational_details.simulation_method: Zener-Hollomon parameter calculation from the Arrhenius hyperbolic sine constitutive analysis (temperature-compensated strain rate)

analytical_models.equation_role: Characterizes the combined effect of deformation temperature T and strain rate ε̇ on flow stress; Z = ε̇·exp(Qp/RT)
analytical_models.model_note: The strain-rate row ε̇ = 0.01 s^-1 and temperature column 950 °C of Table 1 give lnZ = 61.27 for this sample. Qp = 669.844 kJ mol^-1 is the DRX activation energy averaged over the whole experimental range (T 900–1150 °C, ε̇ 0.01–10 s^-1) and was used to compute Z.

unmapped_findings: For this sample (950 °C, ε̇ = 0.01 s^-1) the true stress–true strain flow curve is given in Fig. 3(a); it rises to a peak and then softens to a plateau (peak strain ~0.1–0.2), but no numeric peak/steady-state stress value is tabulated for this specific condition.
This sample lies within the recommended hot-working window for fine and uniform DRX grains, reported as 950–1000 °C / 0.01–0.1 s^-1 (b0012, b0065, b0086).
The dynamic recrystallization activation energy of the Fe-Mn-Al-C steel (averaged over the experimental range) is 669.844 kJ mol^-1 (b0012, b0032, b0085).

The lnZ value for this sample (0.01 s^-1, 950 °C) is 61.27; within the experimental matrix lnZ decreases with increasing T and increases with increasing ε̇, tracking the flow-stress trend (table_001, b0037).

General DRX behavior of the steel: with decreasing ε̇ or increasing T the Z parameter decreases and DRX is more likely to occur, but the DRX grain size increases accordingly; the DRX average grain size after 60% compression increases with decreasing ε̇ or increasing T (b0012, b0063).

DRX degree within a compression sample is greatest in the large-deformation zone (region 3), then the small-deformation zone (region 2), and least in the difficult-deformation zone (region 1) (b0060, b0063, figure_008).
